What gets in the way today

Asset diversion tracking

Historical transfers of assets, intellectual property or investments to related parties before insolvency have to be traced.

Conflicting creditor claims

Lender priority depends on reconstructing a precise timeline of charge creations, modifications and satisfactions.

Strict statutory timelines

Insolvency professionals must compile complete financial histories and asset inventories within tight deadlines set by insolvency law.

Hidden subsidiary networks

Dormant or overseas subsidiaries holding valuable assets can be missing from the main debtor’s disclosures.

Auditor qualification blind spots

Going-concern warnings, qualifications and asset write-downs buried in historic auditor reports are easy to overlook.

Uncooperative management

When promoters don’t cooperate during liquidation or insolvency proceedings, verified registry records have to be pulled independently.

Data from official company filings Secure payments Encrypted in transit

incoinfo compiles information from public and official sources, including company registry filings (in India, our current coverage: Ministry of Corporate Affairs / Registrar of Companies), tax registrations and registered charge records. Reports are provided for reference and due diligence. They reflect each company’s filings up to its latest submission on record and are not investment, credit or legal advice. Verify material facts independently before acting on them.
